what: Casey's General Stores runs convenience stores across 19 mostly rural Midwestern states. It sells fuel and groceries, but it is also one of the largest pizza chains in the United States, because most stores make and sell pizza.
customers: Rural and small-town Midwestern customers buying fuel, snacks, groceries and prepared food.
money: pizza, sandwiches and drinks made in store
packaged food, drinks and household items
moat: Store locations in small towns too small for a competitor to enter profitably, where it is often the only place to buy hot food.
risks: Fuel margins are volatile and a large part of profit
Rural population decline limits long-term customer growth
It pays a very small dividend
opportunities: Prepared food earns far higher margins than fuel and keeps growing
Acquiring independent store groups extends its footprint cheaply
watch: Inside same-store sales, especially prepared food, and fuel margin per gallon.
